treaty_name: Convention between the Government of Ireland and the Government of the Kingdom of Denmark for the avoidance of double taxation and the prevention of fiscal evasion with respect to taxes on income (1993, as amended 2014)
eif_quote: DBO | 26.03.1993 | - | - | BKI nr. 115 af 03.11.1993 | 08.10.1993 | Virkning Danmark 01.01.1994 Virkning Irland Skatter på indkomst og kapitalgevinst 06.04.1994

rates.quote: Except as provided in subparagraph b) of this paragraph, dividends paid by a company which is a resident of Denmark and which are beneficially owned by a resident of Ireland shall be exempt from any tax in Denmark which is chargeable on dividends.

Where the dividends are beneficially owned by a company (other than a partnership) which holds directly less than 25 per cent of the capital of the company paying the dividends, or by an individual, tax may also be charged in Denmark and according to the laws of Denmark on the gross amount of the dividends at a rate not exceeding 15 per cent;

Except as provided in subparagraph b) of this paragraph, dividends paid by a company which is a resident of Ireland and which are beneficially owned by a resident of Denmark shall be exempt from any tax in Ireland which is chargeable on dividends.
Interest arising in a Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State if such resident is the beneficial owner of the interest.
Royalties arising in a Contracting State and paid to a resident of the other Contracting State shall be taxable only in that other State if such resident is the beneficial owner of the royalties.

ppt.quote: Notwithstanding any provisions of this Convention, a benefit under this Convention shall not be granted in respect of an item of income or capital if it is reasonable to conclude, having regard to all relevant facts and circumstances, that obtaining that benefit was one of the principal purposes of any arrangement or transaction that resulted directly or indirectly in that benefit, unless it is established that granting that benefit in these circumstances would be in accordance with the object and purpose of the relevant provisions of this Convention.

notes: Asymmetric dividend article. Denmark-source: exempt where beneficial owner is a company (other than a partnership) holding directly at least 25% of capital (exclusive tier, threshold 25, source_state DK); 15% for companies holding <25% and individuals. Ireland-source: Art. 10(2)(b) allowed Irish tax up to 15% only where a Danish resident was entitled to an Irish tax credit (tax-credit regime no longer exists); otherwise exempt (modelled exclusive, source_state IE). Art. 29(2)(c): dividends paid 30 days after EIF (1993-11-07). Royalty definition excludes equipment leasing. 2014 Protocol only amends Art. 23(1)(c). No revenue.ie synthesised MLI text for Denmark; PPT quote is MLI Art. 7(1) text as reproduced in Revenue synthesised texts (e.g. Ireland-Austria); covered status and WHT effective date (1 Jan 2020) from treaties_merged.json. MLI Art. 8 not applicable: Denmark notifies Art. 10(1) and (2) of the Ireland treaty but Ireland does not list Denmark in its Art. 8(4) notification (OECD MLI positions).
